source: Wenger & Kenett (2025) We're Different, We're the Same: Creative Homogeneity Across LLMs
finding: LLM responses to three creativity tests are far more alike than human responses, even across LLMs from different vendors.
numbers: Mean pairwise cosine distance LLM vs human: AUT 0.459 vs 0.738 (effect size 2.2), FF 0.534 vs 0.835 (2.0), DAT 0.665 vs 0.819 (1.4). Humans N=102 Prolific (114 recruited, 12 dropped). Individual originality about equal between LLMs and humans.
limits: Embedding-model distance is the diversity measure. Alternative Uses, Forward Flow and Divergent Association tests, not blending. Their humans scored lower individually than humans in prior studies.
agent_relevance: Homogeneity is a cross-model property. Switching model does not fix reuse of the same ideas, so a blend step needs its own diversity mechanism.

source: Wenger & Kenett (2025), section 5.3 system-prompt test
finding: Telling the LLM to be more creative in the system prompt raises individual originality a little but barely raises response variability.
numbers: AUT variability, LLMs: baseline 0.459, 'more creative' 0.503, 'very creative' 0.576, 'not creative' 0.492; humans 0.738. Individual originality 0.711 baseline, 0.733, 0.754, 0.702 (humans 0.695). 7-model subset.
limits: Single task (AUT). Only system-prompt wording varied; no temperature or exclusion list here.
agent_relevance: A 'be creative' instruction is not a diversity fix. Even the strongest setting leaves variability at 78% of the human level (0.576 vs 0.738).

source: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich (2026) AI and Its Impact on Creativity and Diversity: LLM-Generated Product Ideas (Study 3b)
finding: Injecting random personas or constraints restores most idea diversity for GPT-4o. Independent single-idea sessions and iterative 'bolder' refinement make it worse.
numbers: Diversity (1 minus mean pairwise cosine similarity): humans 0.773; random personas 0.757; human-picked-problem agent 0.739; random constraints 0.735; chain-of-thought 0.698; random sonnets 0.686; GPT-4o zero-shot 0.679; GPT-4 zero-shot 0.585; bold-refinement agent 0.575; independent sessions 0.452. 100 LLM ideas per condition vs 200 human ideas.
limits: One domain (student products under $50), embedding-based diversity, not blends. More eccentric personas did not raise diversity monotonically. Journal acceptance July 2026.
agent_relevance: Persona or constraint injection is the cheap, measured fix for reuse. Repeated 'make it bolder' loops reduce diversity, so a stuck-state blend operator should not iterate refinement on one seed.

source: Terwiesch et al. (2026), Studies 3a and 3c: temperature, model version, scale
finding: Temperature changes diversity only modestly for GPT-4o. Pooling models and generating many ideas helps more.
numbers: GPT-4o diversity 0.618 at temperature 0 to 0.679 at temperature 1 (settings 0, 0.5, 1). Authors say quality suffers at higher values. Coverage of the 200 human ideas: mean nearest-neighbour distance 0.546 at N=100 to 0.478 at N=1,000 LLM ideas, no plateau; max distance 0.762 to 0.711. Pooling ideas across vendors came close to human diversity.
limits: Cost measured only as idea count; no token accounting. Same single domain.
agent_relevance: Ten times more samples closes only part of the gap (0.546 to 0.478). Mixing personas and models is likely cheaper per unit diversity than temperature.

source: Peeperkorn, Kouwenhoven, Brown, Jordanous (2024) Is Temperature the Creativity Parameter of Large Language Models?
finding: In story generation with Llama 2-Chat 70B, temperature is weakly linked to novelty and moderately linked to incoherence. No link to typicality or cohesion.
numbers: Novelty vs temperature coefficient 0.308 (SE 0.138, p<.05). Coherence loss 0.240 (SE 0.122, p<.05). Inter-rater alpha 0.639 on average (non-expert judges). Typicality -0.095 and cohesion -0.181 not significant.
limits: One model, one fixed prompt, simple stories, non-expert raters, small slopes.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on temperature to diversify blends: it trades coherence for a small novelty gain.

source: Evstafev (2025) The Paradox of Stochasticity: Temperature-Varied LLM Outputs of Structured Fictional Data
finding: Across temperature 0.0 to 1.0, small models kept defaulting to stock names. Rare names clustered at mid temperatures.
numbers: 330 trials, 11 temperatures, 3 models. 'Jane' n=293; 70.4% of last names were 'Doe'; 74.3% of unique first names (26 of 35) occurred under 1% frequency.
limits: Fictional name generation with small local models, far from blending.
agent_relevance: Supports the view that temperature does not remove mode collapse.

source: Mizrahi, Shani, Stanovsky, Jurafsky, Shahaf (2026, TACL) Cooking Up Creativity: Enhancing LLM Creativity through Structured Recombination (DishCover)
finding: Parsing two recipes into trees, recombining them with an edit-distance operator, ranking by novelty and rewriting gave more novel and more diverse hybrids than GPT-4o with expert-picked prompts.
numbers: Novelty (1-5, 48 raters): Exp.1 3.53 vs 3.146 (p=0.0009); Exp.2 3.612 vs 3.141 (p=9.2e-8). Valuable: 80% vs 82% (Exp.1), 85% vs 98% (Exp.2). DishCover supplied 32 of 37 valuable recipes with novelty 4 or more. Tree edit distance 132.14 vs 89.35 (Exp.1). Self-BLEU-4 0.192 vs 0.599 (Exp.1), 0.475 vs 0.753 (Exp.2).
limits: Cooking only. Rater agreement low: Krippendorff alpha 0.201 and 0.209, though IQR about 1.0. The GPT-4o prompt was picked by culinary experts to favour the baseline. Value was slightly lower for the structured system. Not a formal blending-theory system.
agent_relevance: Nearest test of explicit structured merging vs plain prompting. The structured merge won on novelty at a small cost in value.

source: Mizrahi et al. (2026), GPT-4o merge behaviour and fixation
finding: Plain GPT-4o makes shallow merges: it prepares each dish separately and stacks them. It also repeats the same ingredients.
numbers: GPT-4o recipes about twice as long: 24.98 vs 12.3 ingredients, 465.84 vs 240.28 words (Exp.1). In open recipes 56% used smoked paprika (0.375% in the repository), 47% mint, 41% maple syrup, 29% pomegranate molasses. Same-pair cosine similarity 0.90. Temperature above 1 gave gibberish; novelty gains at higher temperature were 'rather subtle'.
limits: One model (gpt-4o-2024-08-06), one domain.
agent_relevance: Shallow juxtaposition is the default failure of simple mixing in text. Evidence that selective projection or deep integration matters in text, unlike the near-equal diffusion result.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction in LLMs (ICLR)
finding: Asking the model to first state the high-level principle behind a problem, then reason from it, raises accuracy on STEM and multi-hop tasks. This is the closest tested analogue of an explicit generic-space step.
numbers: PaLM-2L MMLU Physics 66.4% to 73.2%, Chemistry 70.9% to 81.8%; abstract reports TimeQA +27% and MuSiQue +7%. On GPT-4, plain is 69.4% (Physics) and 80.9% (Chemistry), and CoT reaches 82.9% and 85.3%.
quote: The purpose of abstraction is not to be vague
limits: Not blending; reasoning tasks. The abstraction gains are mainly measured on PaLM-2L. Token cost not equalised.
agent_relevance: Shows an abstraction-first step can raise accuracy. It does not show a generic-space step inside a merge.

source: Zheng et al. (2024), Step-Back error analysis
finding: The abstraction step is itself a failure point. Wrong principles cause errors, and step-back also breaks some answers the base model had right.
numbers: MMLU high-school Physics: step-back corrects 20.5% of baseline errors and introduces 11.9% new errors. 'Principle Error' is a named error class. Reasoning stays the bottleneck.
limits: Rates are for PaLM-2L.
agent_relevance: Matches the Schapiro finding that a valid generic space is the bottleneck. Verify the abstraction before using it.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners (ICLR)
finding: Having the model self-generate relevant example problems before solving beats 0-shot CoT and manual few-shot CoT on GSM8K, MATH, Codeforces and BIG-Bench.
numbers: Abstract-level claim read this session; tables not extracted.
limits: Analogy-and-recall step, not a blend of two sources. Covered by the analogical problem solving subfield.
agent_relevance: Related problem-solving operator. No merge of two candidate approaches.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities
finding: Layered aggregation, where each model reads all previous outputs and writes a synthesis, beats single models on open-ended chat quality. This is merging of candidate answers, not conceptual blending.
numbers: AlpacaEval 2.0 LC win rate 65.1% (open-source MoA, 6 proposers, 3 layers) vs 57.5% GPT-4 Omni. MoA-Lite (2 layers) +1.8% over GPT-4o at lower cost.
limits: Judged by GPT-4-based evaluators; chat quality, not reasoning problems; many extra tokens.
agent_relevance: Only measured merge-of-candidates result found. No result for merging two failed approaches on problem solving, so gap 2 stays open.

source: Lake & Murphy (2021) Word meaning in minds and machines (Psychological Review): GPT-2 on Murphy (1988) emergent-feature items
finding: GPT-2 picks the human-rated emergent property for only 7 of 15 adjective-noun items from Murphy (1988). Extra context did not help.
numbers: Humans: 15 of 18 items had a property rated more typical of the compound than of either part. GPT-2: 7 of 15 correct, and 7 of 15 again with context. Two correct cases may come from word repetition.
limits: GPT-2 only, probability ranking not generation. Murphy items, not Hampton's. Old model.
agent_relevance: The only direct LLM vs human emergent-property comparison found, and it is for an obsolete model. Rates for modern models on shared pairs (gap 7) remain untested.

source: Forgacs, Bardolph, Amsel, DeLong, Kutas (2015) Metaphors are physical and abstract: ERPs (Frontiers Hum Neurosci 9:28)
finding: A later ERP study finds the novel-metaphor N400 effect only in part: present for low-concreteness metaphors, absent for high-concreteness ones. It lists Coulson and Van Petten (2002) among studies with results that 'have been inconsistent'.
numbers: N=35 analysed (42 recruited, 7 excluded). Metaphor nouns -1.17 uV vs abstract literal -0.29 uV (p<0.05). Low-concrete metaphors -1.62 uV. High-concrete metaphors -0.53 uV, no difference from literal (p=0.58).
quote: novel metaphors usually elicit larger N400s
limits: Not a direct replication of the 2002 design. Authors fault earlier stimuli for not controlling novelty and complexity. Page text read to character 100,000 of 107,765.
agent_relevance: Neural support for blending-like processing is conditional on stimulus properties. Treat as weak.

source: Coulson & Van Petten (2002) Conceptual integration and metaphor: an event-related potential study (Memory & Cognition 30:958-968)
finding: Search for a direct replication found none. Only citing and later related ERP work turned up (Forgacs 2015; Abraham et al. 2021 on creativity differences, not confirmed as a replication).
numbers: No effect sizes recovered this session.
limits: Original not opened. Replication status: none found.
agent_relevance: Gap 6, Coulson part, stays open.

source: McCubbins & Turner (2013) blending and compression experiments (search attempt)
finding: Search did not locate the McCubbins and Turner 2013 experiments or any replication. Only Turner's 2001 book and a 2012 edited volume came up.
numbers: None.
limits: Negative search result. Not opened.
agent_relevance: Gap 6, McCubbins part, stays open.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) arXiv 2509.21043, limitations section (expert baseline)
finding: The authors say the 75 lay participants do not represent scientists, artists and creators, who may score higher. No expert group was run. All 35 models were sampled at temperature 0.9.
numbers: Lay N=75; no expert N. Sampling T=0.9, top-p and top-k off.
limits: Authors list a domain-expert study as future work.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 stays open: the 12.8% lay rate has no expert comparison.

source: Xi, Cheng, Soni, Turner (2026) Evaluating Creative Generative AI with Conceptual Blending (EvalEval @ ACL position poster)
finding: Position poster proposing a rubric for blends: completeness, clarity, relevance, understanding depth, coherence, plus execution time. No measured judge reliability.
numbers: No numbers on judge agreement.
limits: Poster only, no data. Says temperature tuning and stylistic prompting raise only surface novelty.
agent_relevance: A rubric exists, but no blend judge setup with ICC above 0.8 was found (gap 5 open).

source: Leemhuis & Kutz (2025) Abstractron slides on generic space and blend quality (ICCC'25)
finding: Search snippet only: slides name determining the generic space and rating blend quality as the main open challenges.
numbers: None.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Confirms generic-space determination is an acknowledged open problem in the formal blending community.

source: Du et al. (2025) The Challenge of Teaching Reasoning to LLMs Without RL or Distillation
finding: Search snippet only: merges several correct solutions into one refined solution, with mistakes folded in as self-corrections, as a training-data construction method.
numbers: None verified.
limits: Only title and first page seen. Training-time, not an inference-time operator.
agent_relevance: Not a test of blending two failed approaches. Gap 2 remains open.
